title: Grateful Dead Live at Eaton's list reads: on 1969-02-15

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy ’69 show with a smoking Dark Star, soaring Mountains of the Moon and an epic Other One.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crystal‑clear soundboard mix (aside from a brief cut on Lovelight) that lets every nuance shine, especially Garcia’s lead work. Musically the concert is described as one of ’69’s finest – Dark Star melts faces, Mountains of the Moon glides into a sublime Dark Star, and The Other One burns hot, with standout moments throughout both sets.

ai_rating.rationale: All seven reviewers give 4‑5 stars and highlight a superb performance plus an excellent recording; the weighted average of show (70%) and recording (30%) yields a rating well above 4.5.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced mix with excellent instrument separation; minor flaw noted where Lovelight is cut, but overall the recording captures Garcia’s tone and the band’s dynamics very well.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Set 1 builds from a tight Doing That Rag into an incendiary The Other One, followed by a mellow Morning Dew and a smooth transition through Dupree’s into Mountains of the Moon and Dark Star. Set 2 continues the vibe with strong Alligator → Drumz → Chant, then a well‑developed Bid You Goodnight jam that rolls into Space/Feedback before the final encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s intro to “Death Don't Hurt Me” is called his best; his tone throughout the show is repeatedly praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Reviewers note a warm, delicate bass that really shines on Dark Star and recommend a good sub‑woofer to hear it fully.
band_member_comments.Drums: Alligator > Drumz > Chant sequence highlighted; drummers are described as entering a “phase,” with specific nods to Mickey’s percussion work.
